solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It could make sage rage (in more ways than one!)

definitions.text: It could make sage rage (in more ways than one!)

parts.words: It could make sage rage (in more ways than one!)
parts.note: putting a wrong first letter on the word sage turns it into rage, and a stubborn, perverse attitude can also drive a wise person to fury

explanation.surface: A remark about what might drive a wise person to fury.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the hyphenated phrase literally: a wrong head (first letter) R on SAGE gives RAGE. In its everyday sense, perverse stubbornness is enough to make anyone rage.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound names obstinate perversity, while its parts literally describe giving a word the wrong initial letter.

clue.text: Functions with old piano in town

parts.note: works means functions, operates
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone's old piano is still playing in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: WORKSOP is a market town in Nottinghamshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Worksop is a town in north Nottinghamshire, so the answer is an example of a town.

clue.text: Plain old boy meeting you in Paris, one to be embraced

indicators.note: to be embraced says the one is held inside the French word for you

parts.note: vous is French for you
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An old lad meets you in Paris and hugs someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be embraced' puts I inside VOUS, giving VIOUS after O and B.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain and obvious both mean clear and easily seen.

clue.text: What could be guaranteed with chop, pounds being involved

definitions.text: What could be guaranteed with chop, pounds being involved

indicators.note: being involved means the pounds are mixed in among the shuffled letters
what could be invites a rearrangement of the following words into something they might become

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A remark about the cash an executive is assured of when fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could be' rearranges GUARANTEED and CHOP; 'being involved' sets L among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden parachute is a large payoff promised to an executive who loses their job, so chop brings guaranteed pounds.

clue.text: Note of bird ascending over top of hill — some divine revelation?

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first part sits above the next
ascending in a down clue means the bird's note is read upwards

parts.note: a pipe is the note a bird sings

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: any can mean some, as in have you any?

explanation.surface: A bird sings as it climbs above a hilltop in a mystical moment.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'ascending' reads the bird's note upwards, and 'over' stacks it above the hilltop letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epiphany celebrates the manifestation of Christ, and the word means a sudden revelation, divine in origin.

clue.text: Summary of archaeological activity is in French

parts.note: a dig is an archaeological excavation
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A report on a French excavation.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed summary of information.

clue.text: Someone who could clean you up, by gum!

definitions.text: Someone who could clean you up, by gum!

parts.words: Someone who could clean you up, by gum!
parts.note: by gum is an old exclamation of surprise, but read literally it means working at the gums, so the cleaner works on teeth

explanation.surface: An exclamation about someone who could tidy you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum!' is a dated northern English exclamation; here it also means at the gums.
explanation.definitionFit: This professional cleans and scales teeth along the gum line.

clue.text: Look at article found in place where colliers once worked?

indicators.note: found in says the article is located inside the former workplace

parts.note: an ex-mine is a closed coal mine where colliers (coal miners) used to work
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone inspects an object discovered in an old pit.
explanation.walkthrough: Colliers are coal miners, so their former workplace is an EX-MINE; 'found in' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to inspect closely, so it means to look at.

clue.text: Marine growth comes from small hard fruit — there's wonder in that

indicators.note: in that means the wonder goes inside the fruit just mentioned

parts.note: a seed is a small hard fruit or grain
awe is a feeling of wonder

explanation.surface: Seaweed is marvelled at for growing from a tiny fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's wonder in that' places the feeling inside the fruit; 'comes from' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweed is algae growing in the sea, so it is marine vegetation.

clue.text: Nasty fool and sweetheart sent back — good!

indicators.note: sent back tells us the fool and sweetheart pair is read from right to left

parts.note: a nit is a fool, a silly person
a sweetheart is a lover

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an idiot and a lover with a cheery 'good riddance'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns NIT plus LOVER into REVOLTIN; G is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolting and nasty are both adjectives for something disgusting or very unpleasant.

clue.text: Animal starts to nurture young and leaves afterwards

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: An instruction for raising an animal's young and then departing.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned African antelope, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Kitchen device brings some happiness to Vera

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A new cooker delights its owner, Vera.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'brings' in the definition; it is only a link between definition and wordplay, since 'Kitchen device brings' cannot stand for a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A stove is a cooker, a common piece of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: The man is unfortunately absorbing one chemical bad for the body

indicators.note: absorbing means the shuffled letters take in another piece
unfortunately suggests the words the man is have gone wrong and must be rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man has unluckily taken in a harmful substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges THE MAN IS; 'absorbing' places I among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Histamine is a compound released in allergic reactions, causing inflammation and other unpleasant symptoms.

clue.text: After page one, one gets put off

parts.note: post is Latin for after, as in postwar

explanation.surface: Once the first page is done, someone is deterred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one gets' after the comma is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone something is to delay it, the same as putting it off until later.

clue.text: Woman being bad-tempered and daughter scheming

parts.note: a shrew is a bad-tempered, nagging woman
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A grumpy woman and her daughter are plotting something.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd means astute or artful, and in older usage cunning, close to scheming.

clue.text: Demeanour with which gifts may be announced

indicators.note: may be announced means the word for gifts is said out loud

parts.note: presents are gifts

explanation.surface: A dignified manner, as when presents are declared.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence means bearing or impressive manner, which is a person's demeanour.

clue.text: Manage to pay for a fine car

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they can stretch to a nice car.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford something is to have enough money to cover its cost.

clue.text: Black sticky stuff making snake come to a standstill

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
to halt is to come to a standstill

explanation.surface: Tar on the road stops a snake in its tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is a black bituminous material used in road surfacing, sticky when hot.

clue.text: Like group of states restricted by top army officer's authoritarian government

indicators.note: restricted by means the following pieces are held inside the officer

parts.note: FM stands for field marshal, the top army rank
as can mean like
CIS is the Commonwealth of Independent States, the post-Soviet group

explanation.surface: A general keeps states in check under an iron regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted by' sets both pieces inside the field marshal's abbreviation; the CIS is the post-Soviet bloc of former republics.
explanation.definitionFit: Fascism is a far-right authoritarian system of rule.

clue.text: Fits gear specially made for certain vessels

indicators.note: specially made suggests the letters of fits gear are refashioned into something new

explanation.surface: Someone fits out equipment custom-built for particular ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially made' rearranges FITS GEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigates are warships, a particular kind of naval vessel.

clue.text: What's in spit surpasses the normal lubricant?

parts.note: tops means surpasses, beats
oil is the usual lubricant

explanation.surface: Something in saliva is better than ordinary oil.
explanation.walkthrough: A spit is a spade's depth of soil, so what fills it is TOPSOIL; the surface wants saliva.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a spade's depth, and digging one spit turns over the upper layer of earth.

clue.text: Short thread extremely light in tone

indicators.note: short means the thread loses its last letter

parts.note: silk is a kind of thread
very means extremely

explanation.surface: A short thread is especially pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts SILK to SIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Silvery describes a bright, clear, light tone, as of a voice or colour.

clue.text: America endlessly involved in old war zone

indicators.note: involved means the remaining letters are tangled into a new order
endlessly means the word america loses its final letter

explanation.surface: The United States was entangled in a former conflict area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts AMERICA to AMERIC; 'involved' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean peninsula was the scene of the Crimean War of 1853 to 1856, a war zone of old.

clue.text: Before Christmas we do things to help us send messages

definitions.text: Before Christmas we do things to help us send messages

parts.words: Before Christmas we do things to help us send messages
parts.note: seasonal greetings are mailed in the weeks before Christmas, but the item meant is a picture card sent with a short note at any time

explanation.surface: A description of the pre-Christmas rush to get greetings out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface steers towards Christmas cards; the actual items are the cards travellers write home on.
explanation.definitionFit: These cards carry short written notes through the mail, so they help us send messages.

clue.text: Chuck out slippery customer seen pocketing ten pence

indicators.note: seen pocketing means the slippery customer holds the other letters inside

parts.note: an eel is a slippery customer, literally and figuratively
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A con man is thrown out after being caught stealing a few coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to throw out or eject, which is what chuck out means.

clue.text: Farewell gold! Pass away surrounded by it

indicators.note: surrounded by it says the dying is enclosed by the gold just mentioned

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to pass away is to die

explanation.surface: A dying miser says goodbye to his treasure, wrapped in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' in 'surrounded by it' points back to gold, so the metal wraps the dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French word used in English to bid goodbye.

clue.text: Monster — fellow with heart traps it rolling over

indicators.note: traps means the fellow and heart pair hold another piece between them

parts.note: a fellow is a man
the core is the heart or centre of something

indicators.note: rolling over means the word it is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A man of courage catches a monster as it tumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling over' flips the little word, and 'traps' tucks it between the fellow and the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The manticore is a legendary beast with a man's head, lion's body and scorpion's tail.

clue.text: My lament: prelate being unstable in terms of emotional disposition

indicators.note: being unstable suggests the letters wobble and settle into a new order

explanation.surface: A bishop's lament about his own shaky moods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being unstable' rearranges MY LAMENT plus PRELATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperamentally is an adverb meaning with regard to one's nature or mood, matching the adverbial phrase.
